chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from al-Ala' ibn Sayabat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) did not validate the testimony of the employee.
ai.seo_question: Why is the testimony of an employee not accepted in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records a legal ruling by Amir al-Mu'minin (Imam Ali, peace be upon him) regarding the validity of testimony in judicial matters. Specifically, it states that the testimony of an 'ajir' (employee/worker) is not accepted or validated, likely due to potential bias or financial interest in the outcome. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the principle of 'Adl' (justice) by excluding those with a direct pecuniary stake to ensure impartiality, a nuance often discussed in contrast to the general acceptance of testimony in other contexts.
